title_candidates: Frontier AI leaders converge on outside testing before release
summary: Leaders at Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind now broadly support outside testing and shared standards for the most capable AI models, while disagreeing on who should enforce them.

primary_source.title: Behind the Curtain: AI godfathers converge on regulations
primary_source.author: Jim VandeHei and Mike Allen
key_facts: Axios identifies convergence around independent testing, coherent standards, and rules focused on frontier models.
The leaders differ over whether enforcement should resemble an aviation regulator, an industry-funded body, or international certification.
A complex certification regime could impose a larger relative burden on startups and open-model developers.

supporting_sources.title: A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age
key_facts: Hassabis proposes a federally overseen public-private standards body and staged pre-release review.

supporting_sources.title: Policy on the AI Exponential
key_facts: Amodei proposes mandatory third-party tests and authority to block releases with unacceptable specified risks.

supporting_sources.title: The US is advancing AI safety through state and federal action
key_facts: OpenAI argues for national standards that can contribute to a wider international framework.

prerequisites: Its model card or safety report

steps.instruction: Find the provider's official model card or safety report.
